newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says franc not overvalued vs mark - paper.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says franc not overvalued vs mark - paper.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday that the franc was not overvalued compared to the mark.

"The franc is not currently overvalued against the mark," he said in an interview in newspaper Le Figaro. He was replying to a call on Wednesday for a sharp franc depreciation by former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing.
"The value of a currency is not set by decree," he said. "It is determined by the markets, in which the figure for France's annual GDP (gross domestic product) circulates every day."

The markets take into account a number of factors and the euro-dollar parity will depend on monetary policies on both sides of the Atlantic, wage trends, budgetary policies and political events, he said.
In foreign exchange policy, what mattered was the currency's stability and whether its level could be justified.
"In a global economy, there is no room for manipulation of interest rates," he said.
Looking at competitiveness indicators in the period 1987-95, French competitiveness in terms of unit wage costs rose four percent compared to its partners in the European Monetary System, he said.
"If the franc was overvalued, the markets would have made it pay the consequences," he said.
